subtopics.title: Free Basic Water — The Policy and the Promise

questions.question: Under the National Water Act of 1998, the Reserve is:
options: Water set aside before any other allocation — for basic human needs and for keeping rivers functioning
The water stored in Sterkfontein Dam
A fund for building new pipelines
Water reserved for irrigation farmers

questions.question: The free basic water figure of 6 000 litres per household per month comes from:
options: The average size of a municipal reservoir
The capacity of a standard water tanker
25 litres per person per day for a household of eight, added up over a month
Half the consumption of a suburban household

questions.question: A rising block tariff means that:
options: Every litre costs the same regardless of use
Water is cheaper the more a household uses
Prices rise only during droughts
The first block of monthly use is free or cheapest, and each further block costs more per litre

questions.question: Access to water deserves suspicion as a statistic because:
options: A distant shared standpipe, or a connection to a broken pump, still counts as access
Municipalities do not record access
Access only counts private indoor taps
Access figures exclude rural areas

subtopics.title: Why Delivery Is Hard — Rural and Urban Challenges

questions.question: Piping water to dispersed rural settlements costs far more per household than serving a suburb because:
options: Rural water must be purified twice
Every kilometre of pipe serves only a handful of scattered households
Rural households use more water
Pipes cost more in rural provinces

questions.question: The rural maintenance trap describes the cycle in which:
options: Villages refuse to use new schemes
Boreholes recharge too slowly in summer
Schemes are built with grants, then break, and small municipalities lack the engineers and revenue to repair them
Contractors build schemes in the wrong villages

questions.question: When rural taps fail, the burden falls hardest on:
options: Commercial farmers
Mining companies
Municipal engineers
Women and girls, who carry water over kilometres at a cost in schooling and safety

questions.question: Non-revenue water — a third or more in many cities — means a municipality must:
options: Treat and pump roughly three litres to sell two
Import water from other provinces
Close its purification works
Charge nothing for the first block

subtopics.title: Big Engineering — Transfers, Dams and Purification

questions.question: The Lesotho Highlands Water Project needs no pumping because:
options: Its tunnels are pressurised by machines
The Vaal River flows backwards into Lesotho
The highlands catch heavy precipitation and stand higher than Gauteng, so the water runs down by gravity
The water is carried by road tankers

questions.question: Lesotho's side of the bargain includes:
options: Free electricity from South African power stations
Royalties that rank among its largest national earnings, plus hydro-electric power
Ownership of the Vaal Dam
Control of Gauteng's water tariffs

questions.question: The Tugela-Vaal scheme is expensive to run because it:
options: Crosses an international border
Uses desalination at the coast
Requires constant tunnel repairs
Pumps Thukela water up the escarpment into Sterkfontein, paying in electricity for every metre of lift

questions.question: The five purification steps in correct order are:
options: Screening, coagulation and flocculation, sedimentation, filtration, disinfection
Disinfection, filtration, sedimentation, coagulation, screening
Filtration, screening, disinfection, sedimentation, coagulation
Sedimentation, screening, filtration, coagulation, disinfection

subtopics.title: Sustainable Water Use — Government and Individuals

questions.question: Sustainable water use means:
options: Using water only in summer
Meeting present needs without draining the future — never withdrawing faster than the system renews
Banning all irrigation
Storing all water underground

questions.question: Working for Water is celebrated as a double win because it:
options: Builds dams while training engineers
Exports water while earning royalties
Pays wages to clear thirsty alien invasive plants, creating jobs while releasing water back to rivers
Cleans rivers while generating electricity

questions.question: Greywater is:
options: Untreated sewage from municipal works
Borehole water with high mineral content
Polluted river water below a mine
The lightly used outflow of basins, baths and washing machines, reusable on gardens

questions.question: Together, Cape Town in 2018 and Nelson Mandela Bay into 2022 demonstrate that:
options: Early, disciplined saving can halve a city's use, while late savings and unfixed leaks stretch a crisis over years
Only rainfall can end a water crisis
Desalination solved both droughts
Restrictions have no measurable effect

questions.question: The daily free basic ration of 25 litres per person is roughly:
options: Two ten-litre buckets and a kettle — covering drinking, cooking and a wash
A full bathtub every day
The same as average suburban use
Enough to water a garden

questions.question: On the staircase of prices, the free basic water is funded partly by:
options: Donations from water boards
The expensive upper blocks paid by heavy users, which cross-subsidise the free bottom blocks
A flat fee on every household
Selling water to neighbouring countries

questions.question: Access is a paper word warns that:
options: Water rights are not written in the Constitution
Access statistics are collected on paper forms
Counting as having access does not guarantee that water actually flows
Municipal accounts are often lost

subtopics.title: Moving a River Over a Mountain

questions.question: Gauteng needs imported water because it was built:
options: Where the gold was — high on a riverless watershed — not where the water is
On a floodplain that drains too fast
Below sea level
On top of a polluted aquifer

questions.question: The two facts that make the Lesotho scheme work by gravity are:
options: Lesotho's deserts and low altitude
Lesotho's small population and short rivers
Lesotho's flat terrain and warm climate
Lesotho's heavy rain and snow, and mountains standing far higher than Johannesburg

questions.question: Water pushed uphill is precious explains why:
options: The Orange-Fish Tunnel flows south
Sterkfontein, filled by costly pumping from the Thukela, is kept as a drought reserve rather than a daily source
Katse Dam generates electricity
The Vaal Dam is emptied each winter

questions.question: At the five gates between dam and glass, the flocs are:
options: The steel grids that catch litter
The bacteria destroyed by chlorine
The clumps formed when dosed chemicals bind fine suspended dirt together for settling
The sand layers inside the filters

subtopics.title: The City That Counted Its Days

questions.question: Day Zero was the named date on which:
options: Theewaterskloof would overflow
Water restrictions would be lifted
The winter rains were due to arrive
Cape Town's suburban taps would be shut and residents would queue for a daily 25-litre ration

questions.question: Cape Town pushed Day Zero off the calendar chiefly by:
options: Roughly halving daily consumption through thousands of parallel household savings
Building a new dam in six months
Importing water by ship
Closing its industries

questions.question: Nelson Mandela Bay's drought into 2022 serves as the control case because:
options: Its rains never returned
It proved restrictions cause crises
Savings came late and leaks stayed unfixed, so the emergency dragged on for years
It relied entirely on desalination

questions.question: The topic's closing summary holds that:
options: Citizens alone can secure a city's water
Neither side succeeds alone — careful citizens cannot outsave rotten pipes, and sound pipes cannot outrun careless habits
The state alone can secure a city's water
Droughts end only when tariffs are abolished
